newsitem.title: CHINA: China stock indices end mostly up on good mood.
newsitem.headline: China stock indices end mostly up on good mood.

text.p: China stock indices ended mostly up on Monday on bullish sentiment despite a renewed warning from the official media that there were signs of overheating on the stock markets, brokers said.
The Shanghai B index rose 0.431 points or 0.59 percent to 73.925 points on volume of 18.47 million worth $9.92 million.

"Institutional buying in selective stocks pushed the index steadily up, but follow-up buying was limited because investors are concerned about overheating in the domestic A share market," one broker said.
Another broker said the index was likely to move up further in the short term, but only slowly given the cautious mood.
Huangshan Tourism Development was the star on expectations of good prospects, jumping $0.032 or 5.61 percent to $0.602 on volume of 1.2 million shares.
Real estate developer Shanghai Lujiazui Finance & Trade Zone Development traded the most on domestic buying, up $0.022 or 2.14 percent to $1.050 on volume of 1.6 million shares.
Shenzhen B shares ended slightly down in dull trade as uncertainties over the annual results of B share firms persisted, dampening buying interest, brokers said.
The B share index shed 0.86 points or 0.53 percent to 160.41 on turnover of HK$68.4 million from Friday's HK$58.8 million.

"I don't expect any big movements in the market before the annual reporting season ends on April 30," one analyst said. Of the 44 Shenzhen-listed B share firms, only five have so far released their 1996 results.
"Investors are confident about China's economic outlook in 1997, which will prevent the index from falling sharply," the analyst said.
On the B share market, black-and-white television tube maker Baoshi Electronics was the biggest loser, falling HK$0.32 or 6.68 percent to HK$4.47 on the heaviest trade of 1.87 million shares.
The Shanghai A share index ended at its highest level for four years on bullish sentiment with fresh capital continuing to flow into the market, brokers said.
The index put on 16.395 points or 1.24 percent to 1,338.058 on volume of 945.2 million shares worth 11.8 billion yuan.
The SSE30 index gained 49.336 points or 1.40 percent to 3,572.409 points.
Shanghai Hainiao Electronics was the star on speculative buying, surging 0.95 yuan or 10.05 percent to 10.40 on volume of 3.4 million shares.
The Shenzhen A index rose 4.97 points or 1.07 percent to 468.99, due to heavy buying in high-priced shares. Turnover was a huge 13.3 billion yuan against 12.4 billion the previous session.
